text:
anya: Heads-up — noticed our latency panel tooltip is saying p95 is 'client' for the new rollout, but the route-level breakdown shows server-origin p95 is much higher. Suspect sample-origin attribution on the tooltip is wrong :thinking_face:

lee: Which dashboard? the rollout compare view or the endpoint breakdown?

anya: rollout compare (Console > Rollouts > my-feature). Hovering over the small sparkline shows a tooltip listing p50/p95/p99 and a single origin label. Screenshot: https://redwood.local/s/shot123 (private)

sam: I think that's the hover that aggregates the merged rollup, which currently picks the "dominant" origin in the rollup record. That can flip when fallback weight changes. We should show a per-percentile origin or at least annotate "mix of origins".

maria: Agreed — saw something similar yesterday after we shifted 10% traffic to fallback. p50 stayed server but p99 was client-heavy, tooltip still said "server" and misled support. :grimacing:

lee: Minimal fix idea: change tooltip to "p50: 120ms (mixed origins)" and add a small suffix line with origin counts like "origins: client 40% / server 60%". Does our rollup payload have origin counts?

sam: It does include sample_count_by_origin in the rollup proto but UI wasn't wired to show it. Query is roughly: ```
rollup = fetch_rollup(route="my-feature", window=5m)
show rollup.percentiles[p50,p95,p99]
show rollup.sample_count_by_origin
```

anya: Nice. Also we need to clarify semantics: the percentiles are computed on the merged sample set (not per-origin). So calling out that percentiles are from merged samples is important. Maybe a hover line: "percentiles from merged samples. origin breakdown below."

maria: UX ask: for rollouts page can we highlight which origin drove the tail? Like a small badge if >70% of p99 samples come from a single origin. Helps on-call.

lee: Implementation note: when fallback weight changes quickly we can get transient flips because sample counts are low. We should guard with a min-sample threshold before showing a single-origin badge. Proposal: threshold=100 samples in the window.

sam: Also watch out for sampling biases — adaptive routing samples fewer long requests in the gateway; the rollup has a sample_origin field set by the router but the merge path doesn't normalize for router-side sampling. That can make p95 look better/worse depending on sampling strategy.

anya: Good call. Let's add a tooltip hint: "Note: sampling may bias tail metrics. See docs: https://redwood.dev/docs/telemetry/sampling"

deploy-bot: deploy 1.3.8 to staging succeeded (job #4721) :white_check_mark:

maria: Can we get a tiny follow-up PR that changes the tooltip text + shows origin counts and the badge logic? I can do the UI. Sam / Lee, can one of you add the sample_count_by_origin to the rollup API response and expose the badge rule?

sam: I can add the field to the API (small backend change). Will add a unit test for min-samples gating.

lee: I'll take the frontend. I'll add the mixed-origins line and badge logic, and wire link to docs.

anya: Perfect. Can we aim for a staging patch today? If not, at least a doc blurb so support isn't misled.

maria: I’ll add a one-liner to the rollout ticket and ping support. :thumbsup:

lee: ETA for frontend PR: 4h.

sam: ETA backend PR: 3h. I'll post the API contract here when ready.

anya: Thanks — marking this resolved for now. Will follow the PRs. :sparkles:
